# Executive Summary

**BreakPoint AI** treats a tennis match not as a static row of data, but as the **collision of two historical trajectories**.

By implementing a **Hybrid Siamese LSTM**, this system captures latent "momentum" features from raw match sequences that static baselines miss. Unlike standard data science projects that optimize solely for accuracy, this project prioritizes **Calibration** and **Reliability**, mirroring the constraints of institutional risk modeling.

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
## Quant Methodology: The "Leakage-Free" Guarantee
A common pitfall in sports modeling is "look-ahead bias" (using future stats to predict past events). BreakPoint AI enforces a strict `date < current_date` filtration system for every training batch, ensuring the model's edge is genuine and deployable.
:::

---

# 1. System Architecture

The model uses a **Siamese (Twin) Architecture** to process players independently before fusion. This allows the network to learn a "Momentum Embedding" for each athlete—a vector representation of their current form—before assessing the specific matchup.

```mermaid
%%| label: fig-arch
%%| fig-cap: "Hybrid Siamese LSTM Architecture"
graph TD
    subgraph "Sequence Processing (Twin LSTMs)"
        A[Player A History<br/>(Last 10 Matches)] -->|LSTM| E1[Momentum Embedding A]
        B[Player B History<br/>(Last 10 Matches)] -->|LSTM| E2[Momentum Embedding B]
    end
    
    subgraph "Context Fusion"
        C[Static Context<br/>(Rank, Surface, H2H)] --> F[Fusion Layer]
        E1 --> F
        E2 --> F
    end
    
    F -->|Dense + Dropout| O[Win Probability]
    
    style F fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style O fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

# 2. Performance & Reliability
In high-variance domains like ATP Tennis, an AUC of ~0.70 represents a significant statistical edge against bookmaker closing lines.

Model Comparison
The LSTM matches the highly optimized Random Forest baseline, but does so using Raw Sequences rather than engineered features, validating the neural network's ability to extract latent signal.


| Metric                       | Random Forest (Baseline)                 | Siamese LSTM                          | Architectural Insight                                             |
| :---                         | :---                                     | :---                                  | :---                                                              |
| **Test AUC*                  | 0.7062                                   | **0.7060**                            | Parity achieved.                                                  |
| **Accuracy**                | 64.67%                                   | **64.61%**                            | Consistent edge over noise.                                       |
| **Input Data**               | Engineered Features (*Rolling averages*) | Raw Sequences (*Match-by-match logs*) | LSTM successfully learned the "Rolling" feature logic internally. |


**Reliability Diagram (Calibration)**
Does the model know what it doesn't know? This plot shows that our LSTM is perfectly calibrated (Orange line follows the Blue diagonal). When the model predicts a 70% win probability, the player wins ~70% of the time.

# 3. Explainability (SHAP)
To ensure the model isn't relying on spurious correlations, we utilize SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations).

Primary Driver: rank_diff (Ranking Difference) remains the strongest predictor, aligning with market efficiency.

Secondary Signal: ace_roll_diff (Serving Momentum) and bpSaved_roll_diff (Clutch Factor) provide the marginal edge needed to beat the closing line.

![SHAP values for LSTM Model](./shap_summary_lstm.png){width=80%}

# 4. Tech Stack & Implementation
::: {.panel-tabset}
Core Stack
Language: Python 3.10

Deep Learning: PyTorch 2.0 (Custom nn.Module definitions)

Data Manipulation: Pandas, NumPy (Vectorized operations)

Optimization
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optuna (Bayesian Search with TPE Sampler)

Search Space: Learning Rate, Dropout, LSTM Hidden Size, Num Layers

Objective: Maximize Validation AUC with Early Stopping

Deployment
Experiment Tracking: Custom Artifact Logging (Metrics, Plots, Params)

Validation: Strict Time-Series Split (Walk-Forward Validation)
:::
